entries.german: Ineuitabilis et incertus humane condicionis decursus tantis mutabilitatnm vicissitudinibus alternatur, tamque dubiis et inoppinatis euentibus concutitur, vt merito in presentis vite lubricitate non aliis íjuum piis et bonis operibus insudare debeamus. Hinc igitur naufra- giosum mundi labentis statum pretendentes nos Petrus et Johannes de Rosennbergh ad vniuersorum noticiam tenore presencium volumus deuenire, quod diuini cultus augmentum et dilatacionem sicientes pro transitoriisque rebus bona inmarcessibilia comparare cupientes de bonis heredifariis nobis a deo colatis pro animabus nostris nostrorumque progenitorum villam nostram Preterslag dictam cum molendino eidem proximo adiacente monasterio nostre fundacionis in Altouado dedimus et presentibus damus incorporamus condescen- dimus et resignamus cum vniuersis juribus et pertinenciis suis ac pleno dominio, prout nos ipsi hucusque tenuimus, pacifice et quiete perpetuis temporibus tenendam regendam et possidendam, omne jus, quod nobis in eadem villa et molendino competebat, in ipsum mona- sterium penitus transfundentes, nec nobis aliquid juris aut proprie- tatis seu dominii ibidem resernantes, sic tamen quod occasione huius nostre douationis in Pombergh, que in wlgari Bohemico Babye voci- tatur, a solutione decimarum, quas antea dare consueuerat, omnino libera et soluta existat. Et quod fratribus vniuersis ibidem in Altouado manentibus semper in spacio duorum annorum cuilibet eorum de vno scapulerio prouideatur, quia pro illis scapuleriis eis deputauimus tria cum medio talenta denariorum Wiennensium in villa antedictu. Promittimus ¡taque sincera fide nostra sine dolo pro nobis successoribus nostris vniuersis dictum monasterium in villa sepetacta ac molendino et vniuersis ac singulis ad ea pertinentibus, quibuscunque nominibus censeantur, nunquam verbo uel facto impe dire uel inquietare quouLsmodo, sed pocius proposse nostro tueri defendere et gubernare. In cuius rei euidentiam et roboramentum sigilla nostra propria et pro mainri testi(m)onio sigillum fratruelis nostri Henrici de Rosennbergh presentibus duximus appendendo. Ratum et datum castro nostro Chrumphnaw anno domini millesimo trecentesimo octuagesimo tercio dominica ante s;nicti Martini con- fessoris gloriosi. entries.english:
Since the inevitable and uncertain course of human life is subject to so many changes of fortune and shaken by events so doubtful and unexpected, in the instability of this present life we should rightly labor at nothing but pious and good works. Thus, mindful of the shipwrecked state of the passing world, we, Peter and Johannes de Rosennbergh, wish by the tenor of these presents to make known to all that, eager to increase and extend divine worship and desiring to acquire imperishable goods in exchange for transient things, from the hereditary goods bestowed on us by God, for the souls of ourselves and our ancestors, we have given—and by this present instrument give, incorporate, yield, and transfer—to the monastery of our foundation at Altovado our village called Preterslag, together with the mill adjoining it, with all its rights and appurtenances and full dominion, just as we ourselves have hitherto held it, to be held, governed, and possessed peacefully, quietly, and forever. We transfer entirely to that monastery every right we had in the village and mill, reserving to ourselves no right, property, or dominion there, except that by reason of this donation Pombergh, called Babye in the Bohemian language, shall be wholly free and exempt from paying the tithes it was accustomed to pay previously. And provisions shall always be made for all the brothers residing there at Altovado, each receiving one scapulary within every two-year period; for those scapularies we have assigned three and a half talents of Viennese pennies in the aforesaid village.

We therefore promise in good faith and without deceit, for ourselves and all our successors, never in word or deed to hinder or disturb in any way the aforesaid monastery in the said village and mill, or in any and all things belonging to them, by whatever names they are called; rather, to protect, defend, and govern them to the best of our ability. As proof and confirmation, we have caused our own seals, and, for greater testimony, the seal of our cousin Henricus de Rosennbergh, to be attached to these presents. Done and confirmed at our castle of Chrumphnaw in the year of the Lord 1383, on the Sunday before the feast of Saint Martin the Confessor.

Concerning the donors’ seals, see nos. CIV and CXIV. Heinrich’s seal shows a shield surmounted by a helmet decorated with roses, likewise bearing a rose. All the seals are in red wax on parchment strips.
